trial_court: District Judge, Alwar in Civil Misc. Case No.41/13/10
case_name: Kuldip Kumar Lal vs Suman Rani
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act against his wife with a prayer to dissolve the marriage. The petition was registered as Matrimonial Case No.29/2008 and an exparte decree for divorce was passed on 27.8.2009. The respondent then filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 CPC to set aside the exparte decree.

legal_principles.principle: A subordinate Court has jurisdiction to set aside an exparte decree and condone the delay caused in filing such application if sufficient cause is shown by the applicant.
legal_principles.held: Whether the applicant has shown sufficient cause or not will depend upon facts and circumstances of each case.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 9 Rule 13

legal_principles.principle: A Court of appeal or revision should not easily interfere with a subordinate Court's discretion if it has been exercised judiciously.
legal_principles.held: If a subordinate Court after a judicious consideration has exercised a discretion vested in it, the Court of appeal or revision should not easily interfere in it.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order dated 21.1.2011 was set aside and the exparte decree for divorce was not set aside.
